inputs.base_revenue_basis: PROPORTIONATE (look-through) revenue, not reported revenue: FY2025 consolidated revenue EUR 119,081m x attributable factor 0.666. Factor = 1 - 0.458 (T-Mobile US minority share of outstanding TMUS shares, 1 - 54.2% DT ownership at 30-Jun-2026) x 0.73 (US segment share of group unlevered owner FCF: FY2025 US adj. EBITDA AL 29,252 less US cash capex 8.9bn less ~85% of mid-cycle spectrum, over the group equivalent 44.2bn - 16.9bn - 2.2bn). Every engine line is a % of revenue, so scaling the revenue base scales FCF to the DT-shareholder share exactly; growth rates are the consolidated growth rates.
inputs.share_count_basis: Basic = diluted (DT reports one EPS). Q2 2026 weighted average 4,814m (H1 2026 interim, EPS table) less ~7m bought back 1-Jul to 4-Aug-2026. Held FLAT: SBC (almost entirely T-Mobile US RSUs) is expensed in the flows, and DT's own EUR 2bn/yr buyback is treated as value-neutral (it is not credited as accretion).
inputs.net_debt_basis: ATTRIBUTABLE net debt AL (leases excluded, treatment B). Group net debt AL EUR 104,352m at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 interim, 'Calculation of net debt': net debt 138,387 less lease liabilities 34,035; T-Mobile US finance leases stay in) less the TMUS minority's 45.8% share of TMUS net debt ex-operating-leases, ESTIMATED at USD 80bn = EUR 71.4bn at 1.1204 -> EUR 32.7bn. The TMUS net debt figure is an analyst estimate (not in the extracted DT filings): each USD 5bn error moves value ~EUR 0.43/share.
inputs.total_debt_basis: Consolidated gross debt 146,707 less lease liabilities 34,035 at 30-Jun-2026 (100% basis, memo only; the bridge uses net_debt above).
inputs.fcf_basis: All four FCF fields are on the same 0.666 proportionate basis as base_revenue. Consolidated FY2025: free cash flow AL before dividends and spectrum EUR 19,546m (FY2025 AR 'Calculation of free cash flow AL') + non-lease interest paid 5,927 (interest paid 7,618 less lease interest 1,691) = unlevered 25,473 'reported'; less SBC incl. equity-award taxes 1,226; less interest received 1,882 = owner FCF 22,365 consolidated -> x0.666 = 14,895. Spectrum is NOT in last_fcf (FCF AL excludes it); the forward capex path carries a mid-cycle spectrum charge of ~1.8% of revenue.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR Note 47: T-Mobile US stock-based compensation expense EUR 926m (FY2024 EUR 701m); DT's own Share Matching Plan not separately quantified in the extracted text and immaterial (total equity credit from share-based payment EUR 839m). Equity-award withholding taxes at TMUS are buried in 'T-Mobile US share buy-backs/share-based payment' (financing) and are ESTIMATED at EUR 300m -> 1,226m consolidated, 1.03% of revenue. The financial-parser extracted no SBC column; this is the analyst's backfill.
inputs.buyback_note: DT AG bought back EUR 2,000m in FY2025 and EUR 997m in H1 2026 of a EUR 2bn 2026 programme (to recoup dilution from the 2021 SoftBank capital increase, i.e. non-SBC). T-Mobile US separately returned USD 14bn in 2025 (USD 9.9bn buybacks + 4.1bn dividends) - those buybacks retire minority shares and raised DT's TMUS ownership to 54.2%; they are distributions inside the proportionate frame, not costs.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and Xetra quote both EUR. USD (~66% of revenue) is translated in the filings; DT guides at USD 1.13. EURUSD 1.1204 (Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-10-23) used only to translate the TMUS net debt estimate and the TMUS market-value cross-check.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 7.0% nominal, built for EUR-reported flows that are ~2/3 USD-sourced at constant FX: risk-free blended 3.8% (10y Bund ~2.9% after the June-2026 ECB hike, US 10y ~4.3%, weighted by flow share - using a pure EUR rate on constant-FX USD flows would overstate value by the rate differential), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.95 (telco asset beta ~0.55 at ~2.6x net debt/EBITDA AL) -> cost of equity ~8.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (non-lease interest paid 5.9bn on ~112bn gross debt) -> 4.0% after tax; market weights ~65/35 on a look-through EV. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the probability-weighted flows, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the margin path is built on adjusted EBITDA AL, which is after ROU depreciation and lease interest (FY2025 4,689 + 1,691; cash lease principal 4,515 + interest 1,691), so lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (net debt AL basis) and D&A for cash tax is ex-ROU depreciation (24,009 - 4,689 = 19,320 = 16.2% of revenue). lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already inside EBITDA AL.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE by proportionate consolidation: flows scaled by 0.666 (base_revenue) and net debt reduced by the TMUS minority's share of TMUS net debt. No NCI deduction in the bridge for TMUS. Cross-check against market: the TMUS minority (45.8% of ~1,065m outstanding shares at USD 146.54) is worth ~EUR 63.8bn at market; the proportionate method instead removes ~0.33 of the group EV the model computes, so it scales with each scenario (DT holders bear only ~54% of any TMUS outcome). European minorities (OTE, Magyar Telekom, Hrvatski Telekom etc.) are deducted in the equity_bridge at an estimated market value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations, on a PROPORTIONATE look-through basis because ~46% of the dominant subsidiary (T-Mobile US) belongs to its own public minority. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US' (telecom operator: subscription revenue, heavy capex, real FCF - not a bank, REIT or holdco). No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: first valuation. Margin path anchors: FY2026 guidance adj. EBITDA AL ~EUR 47.5bn and FCF AL ~EUR 20.0bn (raised at H1 2026); 2024 CMD 4-6% EBITDA AL CAGR and FCF AL ~EUR 21bn by 2027. Engine 'ebitda_margin_path' = adj. EBITDA AL margin + 0.75pp SBC gross-up (SBC is already expensed inside IFRS EBITDA AL; grossing it up lets the engine charge it visibly via sbc_pct_path, which also carries the estimated withholding taxes) - a recurring EBITDA-AL-to-FCF leakage for cash special factors (restructuring, Sprint/UScellular integration), device-receivable working capital and provisions (FY2025 actual 3.3bn = 2.8% of revenue; ~4% implied by 2026 guidance, faded to 3.0%). Year-1 consolidated owner FCF ties to guidance: engine ~EUR 21.1bn vs guided FCF AL 20.0 + non-lease net interest ~4.4 - SBC/taxes 1.25 - mid-cycle spectrum 2.2 = ~20.95bn. Spectrum: lumpy (C-band 2021, AWS-3 auction June 2026) so it is mid-cycled at ~1.8% of revenue inside capex_pct_path rather than taken as reported. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes 1,652m = ~7% of EBIT AL because of T-Mobile US's Sprint-era loss carryforwards; ramped to a 25% blended statutory rate (US 21%+state, Germany ~30%, Europe lower) by 2031. Unlevered tax on EBIT; the interest shield lives in the after-tax cost of debt. Base revenue is FY2025 while the balance sheet is 30-Jun-2026 - year 1 is FY2026, half elapsed; the six months of H1 2026 FCF retained against the June net debt is a small conservative bias. Note that TMUS trades near its 52-week low (USD 146.32-224.75); the bear weight reflects that signal even though DT's filings to H1 2026 show no deterioration.

equity_bridge.item: Investments accounted for using the equity method (attributable)
equity_bridge.note: EUR 11,052m book at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 balance sheet): ~EUR 5.5bn held at DT level (GD Towers 49%, GlasfaserPlus 50%) at 100%, ~EUR 5.5bn at T-Mobile US level (Metronet/Lumos fiber JVs) at 54.2%. Their earnings sit outside EBITDA AL and FCF AL, so the asset belongs in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Split between DT and TMUS levels is an estimate.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests in European subsidiaries (OTE, Magyar Telekom, Hrvatski Telekom, others)
equity_bridge.note: Estimated market value of the listed European minorities (~EUR 4bn at book: group NCI EUR 28.5bn less ~EUR 24.5bn attributable to TMUS minority). Their flows were left inside the proportionate base, so their claim is deducted here once.

equity_bridge.item: Provisions for pensions and other employee benefits
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 balance sheet; debt-like, not inside net debt.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.6% 3y / 11.6% 5y, parent-share) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (1.4% / 3.4%). Book equity is inflated by the FY2023 GD Towers deconsolidation gain and by TMUS buybacks shifting equity from NCI to the parent; it is not an organic growth rate, so the revenue 5y CAGR (which includes the 2020 Sprint consolidation; organic is closer to the ~4% CMD target) is selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 annual rows, EUR millions. Reported FCF (OCF - cash capex) CAGRs are meaningless because capex includes spectrum (C-band 2021). Owner FCF (FCF AL before spectrum - TMUS SBC) is available only FY2023-FY2025: 15.5bn -> 18.5bn -> 18.6bn (2y CAGR 9.6%); SBC is growing faster than FCF (701m -> 926m, +32% in 2025 vs FCF AL +2%), so a rising share of TMUS's reported growth is paid in stock. EPS 5y CAGR is distorted by the 2023 one-off gain (EPS 3.57).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adj. EBITDA AL margin 38.8% (FY2026 guide 47.5bn / ~122.3bn revenue) rising to 40.0% by 2030 on the CMD's 4-6% EBITDA AL growth vs ~4% revenue; +0.75pp SBC gross-up; less leakage 4.0% (2026), 3.3% (2027), 3.0% thereafter.
base.capex_note: Cash capex before spectrum ~13.6% (H1 2026 7.8bn annualised; TMUS guides USD 10.1bn) + ~1.8% mid-cycle spectrum, easing as German FTTH build peaks before 2030.
base.terminal_cap_note: 15x: structurally slow, capital-intensive telco (the 12-15x band); Gordon at 7%/2% would be ~20x.

scenario_narratives.base: Deutsche Telekom delivers roughly its 2024 Capital Markets Day path: FY2026 at guidance (adj. EBITDA AL ~EUR 47.5bn, FCF AL ~EUR 20bn), revenue ~3-3.5% a year to 2028 as T-Mobile US keeps adding postpaid accounts and fiber (UScellular, Metronet, Lumos) while Germany is flat-to-low growth under fiber competition from Vodafone/OXG, 1&1-GlasfaserPlus and Deutsche Glasfaser. EBITDA AL margin creeps from ~38.8% to 40% on TMUS and German efficiency; spectrum is a recurring ~1.8% of revenue; the T-Mobile US tax shield burns off and cash tax normalises to 25% by 2031, which absorbs most of the margin gain, so owner-FCF margin is roughly flat. No credit for a DT/TMUS combination.
scenario_narratives.bull: T-Mobile US keeps taking profitable share from Verizon and AT&T on network leadership and converged fiber+wireless bundles, the 'strong increase' guided for 2027 materialises, Europe/FMC upsells hold ARPU and German fiber take-up rises toward the 2030 coverage target, so revenue grows 4-4.5% to 2028 and EBITDA AL margin reaches ~41.5%. Capex intensity falls as the German FTTH build passes peak. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 17x cap. A DT/TMUS holding-company combination that collapses the conglomerate discount is upside not modelled in the flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The US wireless market turns into a promotional price war (TMUS near its 52-week low is the market's warning), postpaid ARPA stalls, and German broadband keeps losing lines to fiber challengers while regulated wholesale access caps pricing. Revenue grows 1.5%, EBITDA AL margin erodes ~0.9pp to ~37.5%, capex stays elevated for 5G/6G, fiber and spectrum, cash tax still normalises to 25%, and the terminal is valued as an ex-growth utility (1% growth, 12x cap). Leverage near the 2.75x ceiling limits buybacks but is not a solvency risk.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because two-thirds of the value sits in one ~54%-owned US subsidiary whose own share price has fallen ~35% from its 52-week high, signalling competitive pressure that post-dates the H1 2026 filing, and group leverage sits near the self-imposed 2.75x ceiling. Base 50% because guidance has been met or raised repeatedly through 2025-2026. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs both continued US share gains and margin expansion through a competitive cycle; the TMUS-combination re-rating is speculative and unpriced.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Deutsche Telekom as what a DT shareholder actually owns: ~54% of T-Mobile US's free cash flow and debt, plus 100% of Germany/Europe/T-Systems, on an owner-FCF basis (TMUS SBC expensed, leases as an operating cost via EBITDA AL, spectrum mid-cycled, cash tax normalised as the Sprint loss carryforwards run out). Proportionate consolidation keeps the minority charge consistent across scenarios instead of deducting a fixed market or book NCI figure.
key_risks_to_valuation: T-Mobile US net debt (~USD 80bn ex-operating-leases) is an analyst estimate, not taken from DT's filings: +/- USD 5bn is ~EUR 0.43/share
US share of group FCF (0.73) and therefore the proportionate factor (0.666) are derived from segment EBITDA AL and capex, not a disclosed segment FCF; +/-0.02 on the factor is ~+/-EUR 1.5/share
Cash-tax normalisation timing at T-Mobile US: a slower NOL burn-off is upside, a faster one is downside
Terminal cap (15x) binds below Gordon (~20x): value is sensitive to what multiple a mature telco commands
SBC equity-award withholding taxes (EUR 300m) are estimated; TMUS SBC is rising faster than FCF
EUR/USD: two-thirds of flows are USD translated at constant rates; DT guides at USD 1.13 vs spot 1.12
